sections.html:
Lake Charles is the parish seat of Calcasieu Parish in southwest Louisiana, on the shore of Lake Charles, Prien Lake and the Calcasieu River, about 30 miles from the Gulf of Mexico. It had 84,872 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 82,676. Calcasieu Parish had 216,785 residents in 2020 and an estimated 208,466 in 2025. The metro area, often called the Lake Area, had about 240,000 people in 2023.

The city sits on a level plain at about 13 feet above sea level, with Contraband, Henderson and English bayous running through town and the Calcasieu Ship Channel along its edge. Interstate 10 links Houston to the west with New Orleans to the east, and Interstate 210 loops through the south. Petrochemical plants, the port, casinos and McNeese State University keep demand for housing steady.

sections.h2: What did the hurricanes do to Lake Charles housing?
sections.html:
Lake Charles was heavily damaged by Hurricane Rita in 2005, then hit by Hurricane Laura on August 26 and 27, 2020 and Hurricane Delta on October 9, 2020. Laura was a Category 4 storm with sustained winds of 150 miles per hour, and a gust of 133 miles per hour was recorded at Lake Charles Regional Airport. Many local houses were damaged more than once, so a seller today may own a house with a patched roof, a partial rebuild or a tarp that never became a full repair.

  • Gather insurance claim letters and payment records for each storm.
  • Keep contractor invoices, permits and final inspection papers.
  • Note any work that was started and not finished.
  • List what you know about mold, water intrusion or past gutting.

These records answer the first questions a buyer will ask. A house with partial repairs and no paperwork is harder to sell on the open market, which is a common reason owners look for a buyer who will take it as it stands.

Lake Charles is among the most humid cities in the contiguous United States, with average relative humidity of about 90 percent in the morning and 72 percent in the afternoon. Annual rain runs about 57 to 60 inches over roughly 108 days, and summer afternoons reach the low 90s. That wears on roofing, wood trim, attic insulation and air conditioning, and it feeds mold in any house that sat closed up after storm damage. A record low of 3 degrees means pipe wraps matter in a cold snap.

The Calcasieu Parish Assessor reduced values on structures throughout the parish for 2020 after Hurricanes Laura and Delta, and it provides a homestead continuation form for owners whose homes were damaged or destroyed by those storms or by flood. Call 337-721-3000 about your own parcel.

The standard homestead exemption covers the first $7,500 of assessed value on an owner-occupied home, and the owner must sign for it in person at the assessor's office. More than 70 taxing districts, among them the School Board, Police Jury and fire protection districts, set the millage, so the bill depends on where the house sits.

Commercial propertyAssessed at 15%

sections.h2: What happens if property tax goes unpaid before a Lake Charles sale?
sections.html:
Louisiana taxes are due by December 31 and are delinquent the following day. Under R.S. 47:2127, interest runs at one percent per month, and a five percent penalty is added if the tax lien goes to a lien auction. A missing tax notice does not excuse the owner, who is still responsible for confirming the taxes were paid.

If a house sat empty after a storm and notices went to an old address, call the Calcasieu Parish Sheriff, who collects the tax, and ask what is owed before you set a closing date. Back taxes can be paid from proceeds at closing, though the figure is cleaner if you know it in advance.

sections.h2: How a Lake Charles house is sold under Louisiana law
sections.html:
The sale is made by a written act, either authentic or under private signature, and it counts against outside parties only once it is filed for registry in the parish where the property sits (Civil Code art. 1839). For Lake Charles that is Calcasieu Parish.

The seller also owes the buyer a disclosure form by the time of the offer. R.S. 9:3198 allows you to mark facts as unknown, and it protects you if an error was not willful. A late form lets the buyer cancel within 72 hours. List storm damage and repairs on the form as accurately as you can.

After you accept an offer, a notary or attorney orders a title search and your lender supplies a payoff. Have your deed, latest tax bill, insurance claim records and repair papers ready. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection, and a house with open storm repairs can stall that process. A cash buyer can close once the title is clear. Your mortgage balance, taxes and recording costs are paid from proceeds at the signing, so request the settlement statement early.

A cash buyer needs no lender, so there is no loan approval and no lender-ordered appraisal. Many cash buyers take a house as-is, which can spare you the repairs a financed buyer would require after an inspection, and you skip weeks of showings. The trade-off is a lower price than a finished listing might reach, so weigh that gap against repair costs, carrying costs and how long you can wait.

Taxes, any mortgage and recording costs still come out of the proceeds, and the notary or attorney handles the closing the same way.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html: Pull together the deed, the latest tax bill, the name of your mortgage servicer, insurance claim letters for Laura, Delta or Rita, and every contractor invoice and permit. For an inherited house, add whatever shows who has the right to sign. If notices were going to an old address, update it with the sheriff and the assessor so nothing important is missed during the sale.

A listing works best for a house that has been fully repaired and can wait for financing. A cash sale fits a house with unfinished storm work, an inherited house, or an owner on a deadline. Compare offers by what you would receive after the payoff, taxes and closing costs, and ask every buyer to put the closing date and conditions in writing.

faqs.q: Did Hurricane Laura change property taxes in Calcasieu Parish?
faqs.a: The assessor reduced values on structures parish-wide for 2020 after Laura and Delta and offers a disaster homestead continuation form. Call 337-721-3000 for your own parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake Charles house with unrepaired storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Disclose the damage on the Louisiana form, share any claim and contractor papers you have, and expect buyers to price in the remaining work.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Louisiana property tax?
faqs.a: One percent per month from the day after the due date, under R.S. 47:2127, plus a five percent penalty if the lien is offered at auction.

faqs.q: Who sets millage rates in Calcasieu Parish?
faqs.a: The more than 70 taxing districts, including the School Board and Police Jury, set rates. The assessor values property but does not set the rate.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The new owner has to sign for homestead in person at the Calcasieu Parish Assessor's office.
